 Seven Product Recalls Announced for Fire, Choking and Other Hazards
 Free Press Publisher 
 November 12, 2026 
 Notices 
 Seven recalls announced Nov. 12, 2026, affect toys, electric tricycles, portable generators, fire pits, pressure washers and rugs. Consumers should stop using the affected products immediately and follow the recall instructions for refunds or repairs.
 Kakgold remote-controlled car toys 
 Kakgold recalled about 294 4WD remote-controlled car toys because children can easily access button cell and lithium-ion batteries in the remote controls. The toys violate the mandatory toy safety standard. Swallowed button cell batteries can cause internal chemical burns, serious injuries and death.
 Consumers should contact Kakgold at kakrecall@outlook.com for a full refund. They will be asked to write “RECALLED” on the product and email a photograph showing its disposal. Batteries must be disposed of or recycled according to local hazardous-waste procedures.
 Huffy Buzz Bicycles Cerana T2 E-Trikes 
 Huffy recalled about 286 Cerana T2 electric tricycles because the rear wheels can loosen or separate from the rear frame, creating a fall hazard.
 Consumers should contact Huffy for free replacement rear axle assemblies, which can be shipped to consumers or a third-party repair provider. Huffy will reimburse up to $100 in third-party repair charges.
 Contact Huffy at 855-430-6240, service@huffy.com or buzzbicycles.com/recalls .
 Cummins portable generators 
 Cummins recalled about 2,960 portable generators because incorrectly installed valves prevent gasoline vapors from venting properly. Pressure can build inside the tank, causing fuel to discharge or the fuel cap to eject and creating fire and burn hazards.
 Consumers should check their model and part numbers on Cummins’ recall page . Affected generators qualify for a free repair at an authorized Cummins service location.
 Service locations are listed at quickserve.cummins.com . Consumers can also call 800-286-6467.
 Sharper Image tabletop and infinity fire pits 
 Allstar recalled about 265,000 Sharper Image tabletop and infinity fire pits because burning liquid can escape or trigger flame jetting from fuel containers, creating burn and fire hazards.
 Consumers should register for a full refund at firepitrecall.expertinquiry.com , mark the product “RECALLED – DO NOT USE” in permanent marker and submit three photographs as instructed.
 After registration is confirmed, consumers should dispose of remaining fuel according to local hazardous-waste requirements and safely discard the fire pits.
 Contact Allstar at 855-215-5032 or allstarmarketing6861@sedgwick.com .
 SHEIN baby rattle and teether toy sets 
 SHEIN Distribution Corporation recalled about 2,657 baby rattle and teether toy sets because purple and orange knobs can detach, creating a choking hazard. The sets are intended for children younger than 3 and violate the mandatory small parts ban.
 Consumers should take the toys away from children and contact SHEIN for a refund. They will be asked to confirm that they disposed of the sets.
 Contact recall@shein.com or visit SHEIN’s recall page .
 QIOMALA pressure washers 
 QIOMALA recalled 80 pressure washers because their power cords are too short, potentially encouraging extension-cord use and creating shock and electrocution hazards.
 Consumers seeking a full refund should unplug the washer, cut its power cord in half and email a photograph of the destroyed product showing its model number to QIOMALA@163.com . They should then dispose of the product.
 Boshengya rugs 
 Boshengya recalled 83 rugs because they violate the mandatory flammability standard for carpets and rugs, creating a fire hazard.
 Consumers should contact boshengya666@outlook.com for a full refund. They will be asked to cut the rug in half, email a photograph of the destroyed rug and dispose of it.

 The Franklin County Free Press, established by Vicky Taylor in 2019, emerged as a beacon of local journalism for the residents of Franklin County. Under Vicky's leadership, it quickly became an essential source of news, particularly at a time when major newspaper publications were increasingly overlooking local coverage. 
On January 1, 2022, the torch was passed to Nathan Neil and his firm, Neil Publishing, LLC. Neil, a local entrepreneur with multiple thriving businesses in Chambersburg, shares Vicky's fervent commitment to both the community and the world of local journalism. 
Rooted in the heart of Franklin County and powered by its residents, the Franklin County Free Press continues to bridge the gap, ensuring that the local stories, events, and issues that matter most to the community remain in the spotlight.
